Build with agents

Start a task, guide the work, and review the result.

Start an agent task

  1. Install Codex or Claude CLI, then open Settings → Agents → Models. Sign in, choose Check, and wait for Ready. Supported API-key providers are also available.
  2. Select Development and Review defaults. Use a repository’s Model overrides for different choices.
  3. Open Tasks → + New task. Describe the outcome, useful context, and how to check success.
  4. Review Automation, then Send. ByteQuay prepares a separate branch and working copy.

During work, Steer adds guidance when supported; Run next queues a message. Inspect permission requests before allowing them. Stop this turn interrupts the agent.

Check WorkBench → Changes, Summary, and tests before accepting the result. Use Mark it complete when the task is idle and its queue is handled. Archive retains history; Delete removes local task data.

Accounts, usage, and skills

  • Usage shows provider-reported limits or balances, including activity outside ByteQuay. Missing values are unknown.
  • Repository-specific Claude accounts are available only there. Existing tasks keep their selected account.
  • Settings → Agents → Skills → Add skill saves reusable instructions for subsequent turns.

Deliver changes and repair CI

Review Automation before the first submission; the choices lock when the task starts.

  • Auto draft PR pushes commits and creates or updates a PR. It defaults on.
  • Auto CI fix repairs supported failures and can mark a draft ready. It also defaults on and can write to GitHub.
  • Auto review summary adds private notes; it defaults off.
  • Keep commits local for this turn disables publication and CI follow-up for that submission.

Finished development work is committed automatically. Set new-task defaults in Settings → Agents → Workflow.

During CI repair, use @ci to guide the agent when supported. To resume development, choose Stop automation and continue…. Review and merge the PR yourself.

Cherry-pick and backport

  1. In Commits → History, check the first control for the destination and the second for the source.
  2. Select commits or a range, then Cherry-pick. Review the route, order, and resolver before Start cherry-pick.
  3. Follow the run under Commits → Cherry pick. Use Send note or Cancel execution if needed.
  4. When ready, choose Deliver this generated branch → Push branch, then Create pull request.

Cherry-picking starts locally. Dry run shows the plan. PR creation also authorizes the disclosed CI monitor.

For chained backports, configure Related workspaces in repository settings, then use Backport or send @backport example/project #123. Follow Tasks → Backport chains. Each step waits for its source PR to merge; you control merges.
